eva: hey — noticed a bunch of traces with no worker spans for the celery prefetcher queue. HTTP request shows traceparent but the background task spans are missing. anyone seen this pattern before?

chris: yeah that usually means the worker process isn't initializing the tracer or propagators. are you using prefork model?

eva: yep, prefork. we spin up 6 workers. hosted on dedicated infra.

tariq: quick checks: 1) worker logs for 'TracerProvider' init 2) env vars: OTEL_PROPAGATORS and OTEL_SAMPLER_PROBABILITY 3) confirm instrumentation package for celery is installed.

chris: if prefork, make sure tracer provider is initialised after fork (in worker_process_init or on_worker_boot). example for celery (python):
```python
from opentelemetry import trace
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace import TracerProvider

def on_worker_boot(**kwargs):
    trace.set_tracer_provider(TracerProvider())
    # init exporters / batcher here
```

sam: also double-check that the request's traceparent header is actually forwarded into the task args / headers. celery sometimes drops unknown headers unless you set task_publish_retry etc. we add x-trace-id to task.headers explicitly.

eva: ah — we're relying purely on OTEL propagation, not adding header copy. i'll try adding header. any good log queries to find when propagation fails?

otel-bot: try the trace/ingest dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.net/d/traces/celery-ingest?orgId=1&var-service=prefetcher . Filter for traces without span.kind=worker and search for span_count=1.

tariq: Loki query to find worker start without tracer init:
`{job=\"celery\"} |= \"Starting worker\" | json | line_no_tracer = !~\"TracerProvider\"`
(not exact syntax but you get the idea)

chris: another gotcha: opentelemetry-instrumentation-celery needs to be applied in the worker process. if you're using auto-instrumentation at process start it might run in the parent and not the child. prefer manual instrumentation in on_worker_boot.

eva: thanks. what's our sampler config? we see a lot of traces but only some requests sampled so correlation is weird.

tariq: env OTEL_SAMPLER_PROBABILITY=0.02 on prod (2%). but we have per-service overrides in the collector that can override. check collector config at https://configs.redwood.net/otel/collector.yaml (look for probabilistic_sampler processors).

sam: if sampling is low, you'll still see the request span and not the worker because request was sampled but worker not, or vice versa. propagate sampling decision via traceparent — if worker starts a new root, that causes split. ensure worker uses incoming trace id as parent, not start a new root.

chris: short test you can do: instrument a small task that logs the trace id at publish and at start. run locally with OTEL_SAMPLER_PROBABILITY=1.0 and prefork=1 for reproducibility.

sam: command: `OTEL_PROPAGATORS=\"tracecontext,baggage\" OTEL_SAMPLER_PROBABILITY=1.0 celery -A app worker -Q prefetcher -c1 --loglevel=debug`

eva: i'll run that now and report. if that reproduces, i'll patch on_worker_boot to set provider and add explicit header copy.

chris: ping me on the PR, i'll review fast. small patch we used before: add `task.request.headers.get('traceparent')` -> set current context before starting spans.

tariq: one more thing — alerts: if you want to mute noise for now, lower alert sensitivity on \"worker-trace-drop-rate\" in alerts -> change window to 30m and threshold to 5% until we fix. link: https://alerts.redwood.net/rules/worker-trace-drop-rate

eva: got it. thanks everyone. will update in ~30m or when i have a repro. :thumbsup:

chris: nice, and if you need any dashboard links or sample queries i can post them.

eva: will do — marking this thread solved for now.
